title: Self-Taught Evaluators

contributions.purpose: Train strong LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators / reward models without relying on costly, staleness-prone human preference annotations.
contributions.mechanism: An iterative self-improvement scheme that, from unlabeled instructions, prompts a seed model to generate contrasting synthetic response pairs (one deliberately inferior), has the model-as-judge produce reasoning traces and judgments, labels them via the synthetic pair design, fine-tunes on the correct judgments, and repeats using the improved model each iteration.
contributions.evaluation: Starting from Llama3-70B-Instruct, improves RewardBench accuracy from 75.4 to 88.3 (iteration 5), or 88.7 with 32-sample majority vote; outperforms GPT-4 as a judge and matches top labeled-data reward models. Beats a HelpSteer2 (10k human-annotated) LLM-as-a-Judge trained from the same seed (85.6).
contributions.source_quote: Without any labeled preference data, our Self-Taught Evaluator can improve a strong LLM (Llama3-70B-Instruct) from 75.4 to 88.3 (88.7 with majority vote) on RewardBench. This outperforms commonly used LLM judges such as GPT-4 and matches the performance of the top-performing reward models trained with labeled examples.

contributions.purpose: Show the approach generalizes beyond RewardBench to other pairwise evaluation benchmarks and analyze position bias.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluate the trained Self-Taught Evaluator on MT-Bench (agreement on non-tie examples, averaged over both response orders) and HelpSteer2 validation (average accuracy plus position-consistent accuracy over two orders and three seeds).
contributions.evaluation: On MT-Bench, on par with or slightly outperforms GPT4-0125 and beats the seed model; on HelpSteer2 improves both average accuracy and position-consistent accuracy over the Llama-3-70B-Instruct seed.
contributions.source_quote: We find that our Self-Taught Evaluator again outperforms the Llama3-70B-Instruct seed model, and is on par or slightly outperforms GPT4-0125.

self_declared_provenance.quote: The West-of-n approach (Pace et al., 2024) has been used to improve reward models by constructing preference pairs using the best and worst scoring pairs from an initial model. For LLM-as-a-Judge models specifically, synthetic responses have been generated by prompting the LLM to produce a given quality response (Kim et al., 2023).
We consider the setting of pairwise evaluation using the LLM-as-a-Judge approach (Zheng et al., 2023)

notes: Trade-off reported: gains concentrate on Chat Hard, Safety and Reasoning categories while the model is WORSE than the seed on the easier Chat category (attributed to unlabeled training data focusing on harder examples). Relies on majority-vote inference (32 samples) to reach the headline 88.7. Paper decision: reject.
